title: What year one gave
hookLine: the prophets, the Prophet ﷺ, the prayer, the juz', the names, the book

lines: A YEAR COMES BACK IN PIECES.
cards: A year is too big to remember all at once. It comes back in pieces: a word, a story, a habit that stuck, a line you can say without looking.
This path has handed you pieces like that for three hundred and twenty-nine days, starting with one word at the door: salaam. Tomorrow is the lookout at the top of year one.
Before you stand there, let's gather what the year gave, camp by camp.

teach.b: Camp one gave you first words. Salaam and bismillah. Alhamdulillah, inshallah.

Al-Fatiha, piece by piece: Rabb, rahma, the Day of Judgment, the straight path, amin. Tawhid, the oneness of God at the center of the faith. Wudu, salat, the adhan, Jumu'ah, dhikr, Ramadan, zakat, and the Prophet ﷺ.
Camp two gave you the stories. Adam. Nuh and the ark.
Ibrahim. Musa and Pharaoh. Yusuf across a whole surah.
Maryam and Isa. Yunus in the belly of the fish. Then the Prophet himself: Mecca, the cave, the hijra, the camel kneeling in Medina.

teach.h: CAMPS TWO AND THREE: STORIES, PRACTICES
teach.b: Camp three gave you the practices. Salat step by step, dhikr on the fingers, Ramadan and the two Eids, du'a in your own words, the mosque, halal, charity as a habit.
Camp four gave you the text: the thirtieth juz', surah by surah, from the short ones at the end back to An-Naba'.
Camp five took you further in. The most beautiful names, from Ar-Rahman to As-Sabur. The seerah in Medina, all the way to the farewell sermon and the Prophet's last days.
The Sufi path, from Rabi'a to Rumi, ending with dhikr, the heart's polish.

And these last three weeks, the book itself: a recitation that, tradition says, arrived over twenty-three years, then was gathered, copied, dotted, translated, explained, recited in many voices, carried by heart and heard all over the world.
The Qur'an calls itself, more than once, a reminder. In Pickthall's words: "Lo! We, even We, reveal the Reminder." That's what the year was, underneath all its parts.
Not a pile of facts to keep. A year of remembering.

how: There is no single custom for the end of a year of learning; Muslim teachers and students often review what was learned before starting something new, and some close a course of study with du'a.

games.q: you're writing one line from each camp. which line do you choose?
o: the one that stayed with you.
games.why: not the best: the one that stayed. that's what the year was for: remembering.

practice: On paper or your phone, write five lines, one from each camp: a first word, a story, a practice that stuck if one did, a surah from the juz', and one thing from the depths, a name, a day in Medina, a line from Rumi, something about the book.
Don't pick the best; pick the one that stayed.

wordCard.voice: Tadhkirah. A reminder — what the Qur'an calls itself, and the thread under everything year one gave, camp by camp. Today's word.

orig.note: Arabic: a reminder. the Qur'an calls itself tadhkirah, and dhikr, the Reminder.

carryVoice: Your line: a year of remembering. Five lines can hold a year. Day three hundred thirty, and one day left in year one.
